titulo: How a medieval book was made 📜 Part 2 #history #shorts
descripcion:
Medieval books were written on calfskin, with ink made from oak galls. One giant Bible, the Codex Amiatinus, used the skins of about 500 calves.

Sources: Codex Amiatinus; iron gall ink; medieval scribal colophons.

Could you copy a whole book by hand?

#history #medieval #middleages #historyfacts #shorts

lineas.texto: The abbot gave you a book to copy.
First, the pages. There is no paper here. Pages are skin.
Calfskin, soaked in lime, scraped clean, and stretched tight to dry.
A big Bible needs a whole herd.
One giant Bible, made in England around 700, used about five hundred calves.
Then the ink. You crush oak galls, little balls that wasps leave on oaks.
Mix in water, iron salts, and tree gum. It goes on pale, and turns black.
Your pen is a goose feather, cut sharp with your knife.
You sit by the tall window, for the daylight.
You copy letter by letter. Six hours a day, sometimes more.
A mistake? You scrape it off with the knife, and write again.
Your back hurts. Your fingers freeze in winter.
Scribes before you wrote their complaints in the margins.
One wrote, writing is hard work. It crooks your back, and dims your sight.
But slowly, the pages pile up. Your letters get cleaner every week.
Then one winter night, someone pounds on the gate.
